title: Buenos Aires Event Search Built on Real Local Data
description: Turns scattered Buenos Aires event listings into one search experience for finding plans by mood, neighborhood, and time.
constraints: Event data was fragmented across multiple sources with inconsistent formats.
Search needed to understand questions about mood, neighborhood, and timing without recommending events outside the catalog.
problem: Buenos Aires event information is scattered across social posts, ticketing sites, venue pages, and group chats. Details change often, and each source describes events differently.
People search by mood, neighborhood, and time rather than exact event names. Keyword matching alone misses questions such as 'romantic jazz in Palermo' or 'underground techno this weekend.'
solution: Built one search experience where people can ask for events in plain language or begin with shortcuts for Tonight, This Weekend, and Surprise me.
Turned inconsistent source data into a cleaner catalog by importing events, matching venues, improving descriptions, and removing bad records.
Combined meaning-based search with date, neighborhood, and category filters so every recommendation stays tied to a real event.
Added automated imports and data-quality tools to keep the catalog useful as listings change.
result: Launched a working event-discovery product with more than 1,250 upcoming events, 9,200+ event records, and 1,500+ venues.
Made questions about mood, neighborhood, and timing searchable without letting the assistant invent events.
Built the imports, cleanup tools, search, and event pages needed to turn a model response into a useful product.
